findings.heading: Font and alignment / Fonte e Alinhamento
findings.proposition: The English says the centring excludes the left-most hospital-name column ('all columns aside from the left-most column'); the Portuguese says 'Alinhamos todas as colunas ao centro, em paralelo a coluna mais a esquerda com os nomes dos hospitais', which states that all columns are centred alongside the hospital column, removing the exception. The chunk beside it uses j = c(2:8), which excludes column 1.
findings.reader_consequence: A Portuguese reader concludes that align() with j = c(2:8) centres every column including the hospital names, so they cannot connect the j argument to the exclusion of column 1 and will misuse j when adapting the code to their own table.

findings.heading: Column width / Largura das colunas
findings.proposition: The English says choosing a width value takes trial and error ('It can take some playing around to know what width value to put'); the Portuguese says 'Isto pode ser feito arredondando um pouco para saber qual valor de largura inserir', which states that the width value is found by rounding.
findings.reader_consequence: A Portuguese reader looks for a rounding rule for the width argument instead of trying different values, and does not learn that the width numbers are chosen by trial and error.

findings.heading: Create a flextable / Criar um flextable
findings.proposition: The English says the 'All code together' section shows all the code from beginning to end written in one chunk; the Portuguese says 'Se voce quiser ver uma parte de *todos* os comandos escritos do inicio ao fim', which states the section shows only a part of the commands, and drops 'in one chunk'.
findings.reader_consequence: A Portuguese reader expects a partial listing and may not go to the 'Todos os comandos juntos' section when they want the complete, single-chunk version of the code.

findings.heading: Prepare table / Preparar a tabela
findings.proposition: The Portuguese adds a definition of CT that the English does not have: 'os valores de CT (limiar de deteccao, da sigla em ingles "cycle threshold")', glossing CT as 'limiar de deteccao' (detection threshold).
findings.reader_consequence: A Portuguese reader takes 'limiar de deteccao' as the meaning of CT, when cycle threshold is a cycle count, not a detection threshold, and carries that wrong definition into the rest of the handbook where ct_blood is used.
